answer: Cross-signing fails when a ring vouches for itself in a closed loop. Require each signature from an auditor drawn from a rotating pool the ring cannot predict, and forfeit the signers' stakes on any duplicate submission. Thirty linked accounts then need thirty independent auditors, each risking a stake before a payout, so the wharf of clones has no cheap berth left. One duplicated paragraph freezes the haven at once. Cost: thirty exposed stakes and a glacier of dead shells.
